newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico farm boss eyes lifting milk price controls.
newsitem.headline: Mexico farm boss eyes lifting milk price controls.

text.p: One of Mexico's top farm leaders suggested Thursday that the government should lift decades-old controls on milk prices.
Miguel Castro Sanchez, chairman of the National Farm Council, told reporters that it was time to lift strict controls on prices of pasteurized milk.
"It is the best moment to erase controls," Castro said, suggesting that the price should be left to the market forces of supply and demand.

It is the first time that a top agricultural leader has suggested ending price restrictions on fresh milk in Mexico since the government raised prices for milk on March 17 to 3.60 pesos per liter from 2.75 pesos and ended controls on long-life milk, technically called ultrapasteurised.

The raising of prices was always seen by farm sources as a first step toward ending controls. Mexico still has price limits on a hahdful of products, including tortillas, the national staple corn pancakes.
Mexico has been reluctant to free up milk prices because of the inflationary impact the move would have.
